evals.name: bff-aggregating-endpoint
evals.prompt: In our BFF (Fastify + TypeScript, sits between the Next.js web app and core-api) add `GET /me/notifications`. It should call core-api's `GET /users/:id/notifications` and `GET /users/:id/notification-preferences`, drop notifications whose type the user muted in preferences, and return `{ unreadCount, items }`. The user id comes from the session (`request.session.userId`). There's no repo checked out here, so scaffold just the files this feature needs (plus whatever shared bits you assume exist, stubbed) and a unit test.
evals.expected_output: A notifications feature folder split into domain/, data/ and api/: api/ with routes and input/output schemas and a thin controller, a domain use-case that does the muting/aggregation, a domain repository interface declaring only the two upstream calls, a data/ client over core's transport that throws a typed upstream error, kebab-case files with role suffixes, a feature_readme.md, a unit test of the use-case with the interface faked.
expectations: The route declares a response schema, not only input
The muted-type filtering and unread count live in a use-case under domain/, not in the controller or route
A feature-owned interface under domain/ declares exactly the two upstream calls this feature makes, and its implementation lives under data/, not api/
The data/ client signals upstream failure by throwing a typed error, never by returning { ok, status }
The controller does not catch errors to map them to HTTP statuses
Every new file name is kebab-case
A feature_readme.md is included for the feature
A unit test exercises the use-case with a fake of the interface, no server and no network

evals.name: review-planted-violations
evals.prompt: Review this PR diff for our core-api service before I merge it. Be specific about what to change. The diff is in files/review.diff.
evals.expected_output: A review that flags: inline error-to-status mapping in the controller, request.body used without a schema, the adapter returning { ok, status }, the non-idempotent email processor, console.log of the body with the password, the PascalCase file name, the cross-service database read, the domain entity typed as the Mongo document, a Mongo repository placed under shared/, the billing client placed under api/ although it is outbound, a one-file entities/ sub-folder, InviteService as one class holding two use-cases (create, accept) without the *.use-case.ts suffix, the processor in api/ writing through a core/database collection accessor, and the queue options defined beside the processor instead of in data/queues.
expectations: Flags the controller mapping errors to statuses inline (should throw typed errors to a central handler)
Flags POST /workspaces/:workspaceId/invites reading request.body with no schema
Flags the billing client returning { ok, status } instead of throwing
Flags the email processor as not idempotent across its 5 retry attempts
Flags console.log of the request body, which can carry a password
Flags InvitesController.ts as violating kebab-case file naming
Flags the repository reading the billing service's database directly

Flags domain/entities/invite.entity.ts as the Mongo document (`_id: ObjectId`, 'document shape'): the entity holds what use-cases read, the document type lives in data/models/, and a data/mappers/ function maps the document to the entity instead of returning the collection type
Flags shared/metering/mongo-seat-usage.repository.ts: shared/ holds no repository; seat usage read by two features is a feature of its own with a public surface
Flags api/proxies/http-billing.client.ts: a client calling another service is outbound and belongs in data/ behind a domain/ interface, not in api/
Flags domain/entities/ holding a single file (invite.entity.ts): in a new feature a sub-folder appears with the second file of its kind
Flags domain/use-cases/invite-service.ts as one InviteService class holding two use-cases (create, accept) without the *.use-case.ts suffix: one use-case per module, each exporting one function

Flags the processor in api/ writing through invitesCollection from core/database: api/ never touches the database, the write goes through a use-case and a data/ repository, and core/database holds no collection accessor
Flags sendInviteEmailQueueOptions defined beside the processor in api/: the queue definition with its attempts and backoff belongs in data/queues/*.queue.ts
